Johnson and Wales University (Providence) offers an EdD program in Educational Leadership (preparing principals, superintendents, and college leaders).
That program is very practitioner oriented and will not attract the same type of students as a research-focused PhD program at URI.
As part of faculty planning meetings, our faculty reviewed doctoral programs across the nation.
The three regional competitors are UCONN, UMass Amherst, and Harvard.
Each of these programs offer a core curriculum and specific (and very traditional) specializations such as Education Psychology, Curriculum and Instruction, Educational Policy, and Educational Leadership.
This proposal is unique in that it allows students to tailor their expertise to focus on contemporary educational issues (e.g., Language, Literacy, and Culture; TESOL; Adult Education and Workforce Development, among others).

We believe that curricular flexibility will be an important recruitment tool for students.
Minimal additional resources are required for this program.
As noted earlier, the program has operated by URI shouldering most of the responsibility for program management, teaching, and graduate student funding.
The current program is largely taught by URI faculty.
The new program will also be taught by current URI faculty, mostly on-load.
The proposed program budget only includes a small amount of funding for overload and per course instructors (n=4) annually.
The proposal also includes a Teaching/Clinical Professor to teach and manage the program.
This would allow our tenure stream faculty to focus on scholarship instead of program administration.
The budgetary benefits of the new URI program lies in the tuition revenue.
Registration in the current Joint RIC/URI PhD Program has evolved into a complicated process whereby students in the current program register for all EDP-prefix courses in the Rhode Island College e-campus system.

During the fall and spring semesters, students must also use the URI e-campus system to enroll in RIC 000 for a number of credits equal to the number of EDP credits registered at RIC. (But there is no charge to students for RIC 000).
This dual registration was designed to ensure that both institutions maintain students as matriculating (See Joint PhD Handbook, p. 39).
This registration process has funneled all of the AY tuition for required EDP courses to Rhode Island College instead of URI. (Students can register for electives with EDC prefix and those dollars do come to URI).
With this model, the loss of tuition revenue to URI is immense, but provides an opportunity for a new program to bring in significant revenue (with no new demand on college resources).
